about: The first simulated pool on testnet (ops/deploy_sim.py pool): a menu of 5 000 for 45 and 10 000 for 85 USDC, so 1 600 locked (two payouts of 800). Both stages: target 10 %, drawdown 6 % from the start, daily loss 3 % from the day's snapshot, leverage by the rule v1.3. Thirty days a stage, and max_idle_s the same thirty days: the factory needs it set, and set to the stage's length it never ends a stage before its deadline, so the terms name no idle rule. A fill costs 450 ppm, Hyperliquid's taker fee, with no builder fee: nothing here trades on the exchange. Fills at the book, at most 150 bp worse than the oracle (testnet's books stood 77 to 118 bp off it on 11 November 2026). fill_window: 10 blocks until the keeper's --measure gives the number. codes: empty here on purpose; each trading group's code, the address its owner gave and its share go in before the pool sells (ops/deploy_sim.py codes), the shares from the CFO and Alex.
terms_text: Simulated pool, testnet. Both stages are paper exams on nobody's money; prices are testnet USDC. An exam costs the price of its line: 5 000 for 45, 10 000 for 85. Each stage: profit target 10 % of the size, no more than 6 % below the starting balance, no more than 3 % below the day's first snapshot (equity with open profit, taken in the first minutes of the UTC day), leverage at most 10x on BTC and ETH and 5x on SOL, thirty days at most, with no minimum of trading days. A fill takes the book's price, never better than the oracle's and at most 1.5 % worse, and pays 0.045 % of its notional, Hyperliquid's taker fee. Whoever passes the exam starts the stage within seven days; whoever passes the stage is paid 8 % of the size, once, 72 hours after the payout is claimed, which the platform's keeper does as soon as the stage has passed (later, in the order payouts came due, if the pool does not hold enough then), unless the platform's checker stops it before then with a reason written on chain: opposite positions with another account of the platform, or that and wallets linked. A stopped payout stays in the pool for at least 14 days while the trader can object; then the checker lifts the stop or it is final, and the money is the pool's. Every exam is bought with a trading group's code, which the pool's creator sets with the address of the group's owner and the owner's share, none or 40 to 60 %; once a sale names a code, neither changes. When the creator takes money out of the pool, each code's owner is sent its share of the profit taken (what is above the payouts owed, held and kept, and above what the creator put in, less the platform's part) in the part of every price the pool took that its code's sales brought. The platform takes 0.5 % of each price and of each withdrawal, and 1 HYPE to open the pool. The pool runs at least 6 months (184 days) from its opening: before then its creator can neither stop its sales nor take back what it put in, only the profit above it, and only the platform can close it sooner, with the money going where it would anyway. The creator withdraws by a request: the money leaves no sooner than 7 days after it, within 3 days after that, only what the pool can spare then, and never more than was asked; the platform may cancel a withdrawal request; it never moves the money. While the pool is open, a funded trader's payout stays in the pool for as long as the stage runs; the creator takes profit only above it, and above three payouts of the largest size. A share paid to a code's owner is never taken back, even if later payouts take the pool's money below what the creator put in. USDC sent to the pool other than by the creator's addToPot counts as profit and is shared with the codes' owners.
